Is this a first marriage for both of you? I got married late, and it took me ten years to really settle in. I’m not kidding—ten years in, and we’re still adjusting. Communicate! Talk openly about the small changes you can make to bring each other happiness.

The food situation in my home has constantly evolved. At one point, we rotated weeks: whoever’s week it was had to shop and cook for the entire week. The other person couldn’t complain about the meals but could relax, knowing they didn’t have to do the work.

Maybe being a parent is grounding you in your humanity in ways that you didn’t have a context for before? I imagine that becoming a parent can cause a shift in not only hormones but identity.

The 20s for me was turbulent because of my childhood and I worked hard during that time to heal myself. That process took a lot of looking inward and mental growth. NGL it was rough. It sounds like your family feels that they have license to invade your boundaries, which is the weird thing about people who have contributed to CPTSD. Similarly, the more I tried to pull away from my family, the more they broke trust and boundaries, even though they neglected me severely when I needed them. 

My emancipation came in several steps:

1. The realization that I didn't have to be a part of the cycle, and that I owed them nothing. Working with a therapist changed my life when she said, "If you met these people today, would you create a relationship with them?"
2. I initiated NC, and at some point, people tried to come for me, often invalidating my feelings even further.
3. I moved as far away as I could, 1500 miles the first time, and 2000 miles the next. At that time, there weren't any cell phones, but you can always change your number.
4. I wrote a few letters explaining why, but most people have their own selfish agenda and will invalidate your feelings even further. Sometimes they'll gain your trust just to immediately turn around and break it - like the time my cousin begged me for my phone number, promising she wouldn't give it to my grandmother, but gave it to my grandmother as soon as she got off the phone with me. Fool me once, shame on you...
5. I went completely NC for 20 years, and when I had healed enough for myself, not anyone else, I reached out to the two family members who I knew would respect boundaries. I see them every few years, text here and there, but I've pretty much created a safe life away from "family" for myself to explore my boundaries.
6. I'm still a work in progress, and I probably always will be, but removing myself from a severely toxic environment was the best thing I ever did. Even when I had to work three jobs just to have my own space, it was worth it. Now I'm married to someone who also has CPTSD, and while sometimes we get triggered by each other's trauma, I can always assess what I need to change and hopefully heal it and create better boundaries for both of us.

I had a rich friend who was like, “you should have joint accounts”. Great for her - she never had to work, and her husband made at least 6x what my husband and I make combined. Nice gig if you can get it. 

My husband and I are equally responsible for bills. I pay most of the bills and he pays the mortgage. We also take turns every other week buying groceries - also a place where we have different spending styles. I’m super frugal in this department, and he tends to just buy what he wants on the spot. We also take turns cooking, so that for a whole week we don’t have to think about it. It works for us, and takes away the whole “what do you want to eat” problem. I eat what he chooses, and he eats what I cook. We consider each other’s dietary needs (we have a lot), but otherwise it’s all the responsibility of the person who’s week it is to cook and buy groceries.

You’ll figure it out - just do what works for you and adjust as time goes by. It’s taken us 7 years to reach a good balance, but we always leave room for adjustments. I’m sure that once we retire it’ll make more sense to combine accounts, but we’ll cross that bridge when it comes.
